The Spectre perspective

The right beginning
changes what you build.

A brief rarely arrives complete. The important details are often in your documents, your experience and the way you already work. We start there.

Understand the person.

What are they trying to do? Where do they hesitate? We define the situation the product needs to improve before deciding what belongs on screen.

Find the useful task.

A broad idea needs a focused first step. We choose an interaction that can be tried, with a clear question for the prototype to answer.

Make the boundaries clear.

We organise the source material, define when a person should review an AI response and agree which scenarios to check. These decisions shape the experience.

Scope / Example deliverables

Clarity you
can keep.

A project should leave you with decisions you can understand and build on. Open this example pack to see how the brief, boundaries and working guidance can take shape. The documents and depth depend on the agreed scope.

brief.mdscope.mdrulebook.mdreview.mdhandover.md Example project pack5 document previews

Illustrative excerpts for a hypothetical knowledge assistant. These are examples of documentation, not a client project or a fixed package.

01Product briefThe problem, the people, the first version.

Example purpose: Make approved information easier to find. A person asks one question, receives a concise answer and can inspect the relevant source.

First version: Focus on one audience and one source collection before adding more workflows.

02Scope & boundariesWhat belongs now. What waits.

Example boundary: One defined question-and-source workflow, using the agreed content.

Deferred for review: Additional integrations, new content types and a wider rollout. Your scope records the choices made together.

03Working rulebookGuidance for responses and review.

Example instruction: Use the approved sources and show the reference. If information is missing or conflicting, explain the limit and direct the question to a person for review.

These instructions define intended behaviour. They still need to be tested and refined.

04Review scenariosA concrete way to examine the prototype.

Example checks: A supported question, a question without an answer in the sources, conflicting guidance and incomplete input.

Record the intended response, what happened and what needs attention before the next stage.

05Handover notesThe decisions and the next steps.

Example contents: Key decisions, configuration notes, known limitations and the next actions.

Identify who owns the source material and how future changes should be reviewed, so the thinking stays accessible after the project.

A product with a point of view

What it does.
How it feels.

Language, interface and identity are considered together. Brand, CGI and launch work can join the scope when the product needs them.

01

The words are
part of the product.

Names, instructions and feedback should help people understand what they can do and what happens next. The language carries the same care as the interface.

02

A clear path
through the task.

The order of information, the choices on screen and the moments of feedback work together. Motion earns its place by explaining a change or helping someone act.

03

A recognisable
point of view.

The visual direction grows from what the product means. Its name, imagery and presentation should make the idea easier to recognise and remember.

A useful idea deserves a form that makes sense.

One project.
Direct collaboration.

Spectre is founder-led, based in Switzerland and open to international clients. You work directly with the founder, with one selected client at a time.

The work starts by understanding your context. We question assumptions, organise what the product needs to know and test the core idea before expanding the scope.

The personal perspective behind Spectre ↗

Before we begin

Do I need a technical brief?

No. Start with the problem, who it affects and what you want to make easier. Defining the first version is part of the work.

Is a prototype ready to launch?

A prototype tests the core idea. A public launch may need further engineering, security review and support. We agree those needs and responsibilities separately; independent security and legal advice require external specialists.

Can I see client projects?

Current AI client projects are private. Public case studies depend on the clients’ permission.
